ai.title: Shared CLI exit path replaces Freebuff-only exit path
ai.summary: A new cli/src/utils/exit-cleanly.ts module defines createExitCliCleanly, which builds an idempotent exit routine that runs local cleanup, stops engagement tracking, then drains analytics and client log batches with a one-second timeout before invoking process.exit. This replaces the deleted cli/src/utils/freebuff-exit.ts, so every Ctrl+C handler, the /exit command, the project picker's Ctrl+C path, the login modal's Ctrl+C path, and both buttons on the takeover prompt now route through exitCliCleanly instead of exitFreebuffCleanly or process.exit directly. Alongside that, renderer-cleanup.ts gained launcher-PID polling, synchronous terminal control writes via cli/src/utils/terminal-io.ts, and registerExitCleanup, while the launcher now injects CODEBUFF_LAUNCHER_PID into spawned subprocesses.

ai.title: SDK caps subprocess output at 10M chars to prevent RangeError OOM
ai.summary: Added MAX_SUBPROCESS_OUTPUT_CHARS (10M) in sdk/src/run-state.ts. Unbounded git diff accumulation previously hit ~2GB runtime ceiling causing RangeError. childProcessToPromise now tracks truncation state; kill at cap resolves instead of rejecting to preserve collected prefix. getGitChanges logs truncation via logger.info.

eli5.text: When the assistant checks your project's code changes, git can sometimes return gigabytes of output from huge files, which used to crash the tool with an out of memory error. Now it stops collecting that output after 10 million characters, kills the git command, and keeps whatever it gathered before the limit so you still see your changes summarized. The assistant logs when this truncation happens, and you would only notice if you were debugging because the final summary it builds still works fine. This fix is live in the software development kit today.

eli5.text: When you exit the CLI (via Ctrl+C, /exit, or SIGINT), the assistant now reliably releases your Freebuff slot and restores your terminal before reporting any fatal error. This happens synchronously and best-effort, skipping the normal React unmount so cleanup completes even if the interface is mid-render. You'd notice the difference if the process was about to hang: a session API request that would otherwise pin the 'Starting…' spinner for up to 300 seconds now times out after 20 seconds, allowing the exit handler to take over.

ai.title: Safe JSON serialization for chat checkpoint saves
ai.summary: Adds `cli/src/utils/safe-json.ts` providing `serializeForPersistence`, which tries a plain `JSON.stringify` and on failure retries with a cycle-breaking replacer, and on OOM errors also truncates oversized leaf strings, returning a `SerializeFallbackReport` describing what changed. `run-state-storage.ts` now routes both `saveChatState` and `saveChatStateAsync` through `serializeChatState`, serializing `run-state.json` and `chat-messages.json` independently so a poisoned payload in one cannot block the other, and logs fallback diagnostics at most once per `SAVE_LOG_INTERVAL_MS` (5 minutes) per chat dir. A new `shouldSampleByKey(key, rate)` export is added to `common/src/util/analytics-sampling.ts` for deterministic per-key sampling of high-volume events.
ai.evidence: New file `cli/src/utils/safe-json.ts` exports `serializeForPersistence`, `classifyStringifyError`, `SerializeResult`, and `SerializeFallbackReport`; `cli/src/utils/run-state-storage.ts` imports these and routes `saveChatState` and `saveChatStateAsync` through a new `serializeChatState` that serializes the run-state and messages independently and logs fallback diagnostics, while reusing `classifyStringifyError` from the new module. The diff also adds a new exported `shouldSampleByKey` function to `common/src/util/analytics-sampling.ts`.

facts: Bun/undici can throw when a response body is severed instead of ending the iterator cleanly. Feed that through the same capped continuation path as a clean end without a finish marker.
These final-result promises can reject with the same transport error. Observe them now so the recovery yield below cannot leave an unhandled rejection while the consumer starts the continuation step.

Error chunks are usually model/tool/API failures. Some runtimes surface a response-body transport drop here instead of rejecting iterator.next; the final branch below recognizes that one recoverable exception.
A transport error can also arrive as an AI SDK error chunk instead of making iterator.next() reject. Recover both runtime shapes identically.
A thrown response body has no reliable final metadata to collect. The recovery chunk above preserves partial output and forces a fresh agent step, which continues from that saved context.

entries.summary: SDK changes across 2 file(s) (+147/−58).

ai.title: SDK stream recovery for thrown transport errors
ai.summary: Added `classifyThrownStreamRecovery` to handle Bun/undici response body severing via `iterator.next()` exceptions. `promptAiSdkStream` now catches these throws, classifies them as transient network errors, and triggers the same capped continuation path as clean stream ends. This prevents unhandled rejections from final-result promises and ensures partial output is preserved for fresh agent steps.

eli5.text: You may have noticed the app getting cut off or erroring out partway through a long response, especially if you're using it through a desktop or SDK integration, where network hiccups or runtime quirks (like Bun or certain Node setups) could cause the stream of words to drop suddenly instead of ending cleanly. Now, instead of crashing or losing what was already generated, the system detects that kind of interruption, treats it like a temporary network blip, saves whatever partial output you got so far, and quietly restarts from that point, so your conversation keeps going without you losing context or seeing a hard failure. This only affects scenarios where the response comes as a live stream of text and the connection gets severed mid-sentence; it doesn't change how finished answers are
